author: gpt-5.6-luna
brief: Phase: security. Role: developer. Repo kind: a Node.js 24 document-sharing service (no dependencies, node:http) with handlers to upload a file into the caller's folder, download by path, list a folder, and import a simple archive (an in-repo minimal archive format with a reader, so no dependency) that unpacks into the folder. The handler functions are exported and take a storage root, the caller's user id and the request input, so tests can call them directly. The request quotes a bug bounty report: a researcher read another user's files and wrote outside their own folder; no detail. Defects to seed: download joins the user's root with the query path without normalizing (../, percent-encoded dots, backslashes after decoding, absolute paths); the containment check uses a plain string startsWith, so /data/users/ann matches /data/users/anna; symlinks inside a user folder are followed out of it; archive import writes entries whose names hold ../ or start with / (zip slip); upload accepts names with control characters or path separators and silently overwrites an existing file without the overwrite flag; list errors include other users' folder names. The request: close these holes without breaking normal use (nested folders, unicode names, names with several dots like report..final.pdf). Hidden tests call the exported handlers with attack and normal inputs against a temp storage root and check the file system state and the responses.
